channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: The Euro takes a priced-in hike into a week that belongs to American inflation
item.description: 1.1000 has turned EUR/USD back in each of the past three sessions, and it did so in a week when most of the news leaned the Euro's way. Eurozone core inflation was revised higher, the ZEW sentiment survey beat its forecast, and the US factory numbers missed.

item.title: The British Pound goes into PMI week paying for softer inflation and slower pay
item.description: UK inflation and pay growth both came in under forecast, which is good news for British households and was the reason the Pound fell.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average drops for a fifth day as AI rout widens
item.description: Five falls in five sessions have taken the Dow Jones Industrial Average more than 10% below its August record close, and the selling is no longer confined to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. The index dropped to just under 48,000, its lowest since April, and is trading near 48,100.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Brief dip against US Dollar prompts controls - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister reports an unusual, sudden jump in USD/CNY without a corresponding Dollar move, which some linked to a recent US-Russia-China summit.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Chip export curbs and yields pressure MYR against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong report that new US export restrictions on advanced AI chips have driven USD/MYR above 4.11, overshadowing stronger Malaysian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual appreciation under tight management – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Jackit Wong sees the Chinese Yuan on a path of gradual, closely managed appreciation supported by Renminbi (RMB) internationalization. The recent FX reserve requirement hike is interpreted as moderating the pace of Chinese Yuan (CNY) gains rather than reversing the trend.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains under pressure as Fed and RBA outlooks diverge
item.description: AUD/USD extends losses on Friday as a sell-off in global equities dampens market sentiment and weighs on risk-sensitive currencies such as the Australian Dollar (AUD), even as falling Treasury yields take some steam out of the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Stable range persists as growth outpaces FX – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao and Charlie Lay highlight that Malaysia’s strong Q3 GDP and favourable 2027 outlook have not translated into a stronger Ringgit. USD-MYR has traded between 4.00 and 4.15 for six months, with Bank Negara Malaysia seen comfortable with stability.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI measures cushion losses against US Dollar - OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Bank Indonesia’s (BI) 25bp hike to 6.00% and enhanced FX hedging incentives have helped temper depreciation pressures on the Rupiah despite a firm US Dollar (USD) and high US yields.

item.title: Bank of Korea: Tightening bias holds into November – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research expects the Bank of Korea (BoK) to raise its policy rate by 25bp to 3.25% at the November 26 meeting, despite acknowledging a close decision. The team highlights solid exports, firm PMIs and inflation above target as key drivers.

item.title: Canadian retail sales give the Loonie a pause at a 19-month low
item.description: Seven gains in eight sessions took USD/CAD to a 19-month high on Thursday, and Friday's pullback has given back very little of them. The pair has slipped from just above 1.4350 and hasn't traded below Thursday's low.

item.title: Pound steadies at 12-month low after UK retail sales beat
item.description: A stronger UK retail sales number and a drop in US inflation expectations have given the Pound a pause, and not much more than that. GBP/USD fell to just below 1.3100, its lowest in a year, and is trading back just above that level.

item.title: Hong Kong: Policy support drives cautious re-engagement – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Jackit Wong highlights that Hong Kong equities are the clearest near-term beneficiary of China’s broadened but still targeted policy support.

item.title: Gold heads for worst week since March as Fed rate hike bets and forced selling weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades under pressure on Friday, hitting its lowest level since September 2025 in Asian trading. A sell-off in global equities fuels volatility across financial markets as Anthropic’s record IPO does little to ease concerns about stretched AI valuations.

item.title: Euro edges higher as US Dollar eases, still set for third weekly loss
item.description: EUR/USD trades on the front foot on Friday as a modest pullback in the US Dollar (USD) puts the brakes on the Euro’s (EUR) decline after the pair fell to levels last seen in May 2025 earlier this week.

item.title: Gold: Bull case shaken yet intact – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that Gold has suffered intensified selling on risk-off flows and a hawkish Federal Reserve profile, with CTAs already short and discretionary length likely reduced. However, they argue this does not mark a full capitulation of Gold’s bullish theme, as structural concerns over equities, fiscal dominance and stagflation still underpin longer-term upside, while resilient ETF holdings and potential CTA short-covering may offer near-term relief.

item.title: Canada: Modest Q4 growth expected despite Q3 weakness - RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Claire Fan and Annie Zheng assess early Q4 data for Canada, noting that manufacturing and wholesale sales estimates for October will give a first read on activity after Q3 stagnation.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD eyes 200-week SMA amid sustained selling pressure
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its sell-off on Friday, slipping to levels last seen in September 2025. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $42, about 65% below its January record high near $121, and is on track for its worst week since March.

item.title: Euro area: Moderate PMI growth with French risk – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen expects Euro area PMIs next week to signal continued moderate growth, with the composite index slipping slightly from 51.7 to 51.4.

item.title: Malaysia: Record trade surplus with rising external risks – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Julia Goh and Loke Siew Ting highlight that Malaysia’s total trade and trade surplus hit record highs in October 2026, driven by strong exports of E&E and energy-related products and broad-based import growth.

item.title: Singapore: Growth and inflation outlook steady into 2027 – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s economics team expects Singapore’s October 2026 inflation to ease, with both headline and core measures drifting below 2% year-on-year on favourable base effects. Industrial production is projected to slow sharply on high base effects, while 3Q26 GDP is likely to be revised higher. The government’s 2027 growth forecast is seen in a 2.5–4.5% range.

item.title: Japanese Yen outperforms as global stock sell-off lifts safe-haven demand
item.description: USD/JPY falls on Friday as a sharp sell-off in global equities rattles financial markets and boosts safe-haven demand for the Japanese Yen (JPY), which is outperforming all of its major peers. A softer US Dollar (USD) adds to the pressure on the pair.

item.title: China: Policy backstop offsets weak macro – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Jackit Wong argues that Chinese equity markets are supported by a coordinated policy backstop, even as macro data remain weak. The PBOC’s relending facilities, state-linked buying and new actively managed ETFs are described as sentiment-supportive rather than a reflation pivot.

item.title: British Pound: More upside versus EUR than USD – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that GBP/USD has bounced back above 1.3100 after briefly touching a one‑year low. Haddad notes that stronger‑than‑expected UK October retail sales support expectations for a December Bank of England (BoE) rate hike. The bank sees greater upside for the British Pound (GBP) against the Euro (EUR) than against the US Dollar (USD), given differing central bank outlooks.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: HUF pressured by MNB stance and inflation doubts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose argues that the Hungarian central bank’s dovish stance, framed by talk of improved risk premia and euro adoption, has become a liability for the Forint.

item.title: Euro: Cross-border capital flows support the currency – MUFG
item.description: Derek Halpenny at MUFG highlights that ECB balance of payments data show supportive Euro flows in 2026, with current account, FDI and portfolio accounts collectively positive. The Euro-zone maintains a sizeable current account surplus, while equity inflows and a turnaround in bond flows point to solid foreign investor appetite for Euro-zone assets on a year-to-date basis.

item.title: US Dollar Index (DXY) hesitates below 104.00 as AI jitters offset Fed hiking bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is trimming daily losses during the European session on Friday but maintains a moderate bearish tone, as a selloff in AI stocks starts to hit the Greenback.

item.title: US 10-year Treasury yield slips below 5% as global equity rout deepens
item.description: US Treasury yields fall across the curve on Friday, extending their weekly decline as a sharp sell-off in global equities drives demand for government bonds. The benchmark 10-year yield trades at 4.98%, down more than 13 basis points so far this week.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Market prices in December and January hikes – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Molly Schwartz notes that OIS pricing now reflects expectations for a full Federal Reserve rate hike in December and a high probability of another move in January.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer jobs data fuel rate-cut speculation – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke notes that weak Australian labour market data, including a 43,500 fall in employment and a rise in unemployment to 4.9%, reinforce expectations that the RBA’s hiking cycle has ended. Markets now price rate cuts by 2027, and upcoming inflation data will be crucial for AUD, with downside risk if figures validate easing expectations.
